content.title: Hain Celestial must face renewed 'channel stuffing' lawsuit, US appeals court says
content.summary: A federal appeals court revived a lawsuit on Monday accusing Hain Celestial Group of defrauding shareholders by concealing an alleged "channel stuffing" scheme to inflate revenue and its stock price. Reversing a trial judge's dismissal, the 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in Manhattan said shareholders plausibly alleged that the organic and natural foods company and four executives intended to deceive them about its financial results and compliance with accounting principles. Hain products include Terra and Garden of Eatin' chips, Earth's Best baby food and Celestial Seasonings tea.
